headline: Mechanistic models link reproduction numbers, contact structure and heterogeneity
label: Mechanistic Inference For Epidemic Dynamics
synthesis: The dominant thread is how structural assumptions in mechanistic population models determine what is inferred. One preprint proves that instantaneous renewal-equation and mechanistic SEIR reproduction numbers coincide under homogeneous mixing. A second preprint develops a multi-type branching likelihood for contact transmission trees, validated on simulations and COVID-19 data from Karnataka. A published study finds that random-mixing contacts in agent-based models match empirical surveys for households, schools and workplaces but miss age-structured contacts outside these settings. Separately, a published Bayesian hierarchical ODE framework partitions inter- and intra-experimental heterogeneity in flow cytometry snapshot data, with simulations. What is new is formal treatment of where structural assumptions bind: an equivalence result, a typed likelihood checked against simulations and surveillance data, and a survey benchmark for contact structure.
